introductoryTafseer: Surah An-Nas forms the concluding seal of the Holy Qur'an together with Surah Al-Falaq, collectively designated as Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (The Twin Surahs of Divine Refuge). Mufti Muhammad Shafi notes in Ma'ariful Qur'an that whereas Surah Al-Falaq seeks protection against external calamities of the material and occult worlds, Surah An-Nas seeks protection against the far more lethal spiritual peril: insidious whispers (Waswasah) aimed at corrupting human faith and intention.

sections.title: Refuge in the Sovereign Lord from Insidious Whisperers
sections.arabicText: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ ۝١ مَلِكِ النَّاسِ ۝٢ إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ ۝٣ مِن شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ ۝٤ الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ ۝٥ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ ۝٦
sections.translation: Say: 'I seek refuge with the [Rabb] (Lord and Cherisher) of mankind. The Sovereign King of mankind. The True God and Object of Worship of mankind. From the malice of the retreating whisperer ([Al-Waswas Al-Khannas]), who casts insidious suggestions into the hearts of mankind—from among jinn and men.'

phraseCards.englishPhrase: Say: I seek sanctuary with the Lord and Evolver of humanity,

vocabulary.grammarNote: Fleeing from danger to an almighty protector.
Singled out here because humanity is the specific target of demonic sabotage.

phraseCards.englishPhrase: from the evil of the covert whisperer who slinks away,

vocabulary.grammarNote: Repetitive onomatopoeic root denoting soft, repeated insidious prompting.

vocabulary.meaning: The one who shrinks back and retreats
vocabulary.grammarNote: Satan retreats whenever the servant engages in the Dhikr (remembrance) of Allah.

sections.commentary:
Mufti Muhammad Shafi explains why three divine attributes—Rabb (Sustainer), Malik (King), and Ilah (God)—are invoked sequentially before naming the single threat being repelled. This teaches the gravity of spiritual health: physical injury harms worldly life, but seduced loss of faith leads to eternal perdition.

'Al-Khannas' is Satan's defining trait: whenever a servant remembers Allah, Satan shrinks, retreats, and withers; but the moment human vigilance lapses, he lunges forward to whisper doubts, pride, and despair.

Crucially, the final verse clarifies: 'from among jinn and men'. Demonic whispers come not only from unseen spirits, but also from corrupt human companions, cynical writers, and toxic influencers who glamorize vice and sow doubt.

subsections.title: Remembrance (Dhikr) as the Unbreakable Fortress
subsections.content: Ibn Abbas stated: 'Satan is crouched upon the heart of the son of Adam. When he remembers Allah, Satan cowers and slinks away (Khanasa); but when he becomes heedless, he casts whispered poison.' Hence, the antidote to Waswasah is constant, conscious remembrance.

curatedTerms.literalMeaning: A faint, repetitive rustle or whisper.
curatedTerms.theologicalContext: Subtle promptings directed at human psychology urging toward doubt, vanity, procrastination in good deeds, and despair in divine mercy.
